thread.title: Senator Chuck Payne backs centralized PFAS litigation effort in Georgia
thread.title_full: Senator Chuck Payne backs centralized PFAS litigation effort in Georgia

author: Peach Tree Times
title: Senator Chuck Payne backs centralized PFAS litigation effort in Georgia
text:
Senator Chuck Payne (R–Dalton) has expressed his support for Senate Bill 577, known as the “Coordinating PFAS Remediation Act.” The bill, sponsored by Senator Sam Watson (R–Moultrie), seeks to centralize all lawsuits related to PFAS contamination brought by Georgia state and local governments. If enacted, it would give the Georgia Environmental Protection Division (EPD) authority to manage these lawsuits and allocate any resulting settlement or judgment funds.
“We are all affected by the quality of our water, soil and air, no matter which part of Georgia we call home,” said Sen. Payne. “River water and the water table are not local issues, so the state needs to be involved. This legislation will maximize our ability to recover cleanup costs and invest those dollars back into protecting our communities and water systems. I am proud to stand with my colleagues and take a responsible approach to safeguard Georgia’s natural resources for generations to come.”
The proposed legislation is similar to laws in other states where attorneys general have taken charge of PFAS-related litigation. SB 577 is currently under review in the Senate Committee on Natural Resources and the Environment.
Senator Payne chairs the Senate Committee on Veterans, Military, and Homeland Security. He represents Georgia’s 54th Senate District, which includes Murray and Whitfield counties along with part of Gordon County.
Senator John F. Kennedy also has a history of legislative sponsorship and committee work as a state senator according to his official profile. Kennedy served as President Pro Tempore, chaired the Administrative Affairs Committee, participated ex-officio in several other committees including Ethics, Finance, Health and Human Services, and Rules; he represented Georgia’s 18th District after being sworn into office on January 12, 2015. His Atlanta office was located at 305-B CLOB (source).
For more information about SB 577 or media inquiries regarding Senator Payne’s legislative activities, contact details are available through official channels.
